recipes.name: Cowboy Mashed Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 1 (10 ounce) package frozen white corn, thawed

steps.text: Place potatoes, carrots, garlic, and jalapeño in a large pot and cover with water; bring to a boil over high heat. Cook until potatoes are tender, 15 to 20 minutes. Drain.
Add corn and butter; mash until butter melts and potatoes reach desired texture. Stir in cheese, salt, and black pepper. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Cowboy Mashed Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: Easy, buttery cowboy mashed potatoes combine the flavors of red and Yukon Gold potatoes, corn, jalapeño, carrots, and cheese for a rustic side dish recipe.

review.reviewBody: I have to admit my expectations were pretty low for this recipe despite the reviews. It just sounded kind of strange and I didn't think it would turn out with a nice consitency with no milk, cream, sour cream, etc. I was very wrong and the reviews were right. I don't usually make mashed potatoes because they are trouble. This recipe is super simple. No peeling potatoes, no guessing how much milk to add, no endless mashing with lumps remaining. This came together like magic. Just boil, drain, and mash with butter and cheese. A great addition to my recipe box and a terrific way to use up fresh produce at the end of the week! Boiling the garlic with the potatoes is genius as well. Try this even if you are skeptical. You won't be disappointed!

This makes such a good side dish because you can add or take away what veggies you like..(a good way to get the kiddos to eat them too!!) For those of you who found this to be a little on the dry side...try adding some cream cheese or sour cream. This usually keeeps the potatoes "silky". Thanks for the fun new twist on potatoes Bruticus.

I omitted the pepper as I was serving this with Herbed Pork Chops in Mushroom Sauce, I didn't think it would go well together. I used all red potatoes as that was what was on sale today and added more cheese, and a 1/4 c. hot milk to loosen the mash up a little. (It was quite thick.) I liked these, my family was indifferent. I don't think they liked corn in their potatoes. I'd like to try this again with Mexi Corn and the jalapenos.

Great new way to spice up mashed potatoes. Served with our pork chop meal tonight and was enjoyed by all. I used 1/2 green bell pepper, which I added to the boiling potatoes about 5 minutes before they were done. Once it came time to mash, used a little more butter than called for, added a can of drained green chiles, yellow/sweet corn instead of white and a little more cheese. The result? Great!! Will make these again! Very colorful too! Makes the whole table look "pretty."

It's so simple, I'm almost embarrased I didn't think of it. I added WAY more garlic, and had to omit the corn because I was out (will definitely add it next time). Used real butter, but only about 3 tablespoons, plus about 1/3 cup milk and sharp cheddar. My kids and husband loved it! Boy, I sure did too! This will be a regular on our dinner table. (And, the name DOES help with preschoolers.)

Boy did my family love these. We are potato freaks anyways. This just brought it up a notch. I added lots more garlic as we love that too. Other than that made them just the way the recipe called for. I did double the recipe and they made great potato cakes on the grill the next morning.

I made this this first time pretty close to what's written only all I had was yukon gold potatoes and I left out the jalapeno peppers. It came out excellent and everyone loved it! I have made it many times since. I usually just make my mashed potatoes as I normally would (yukon gold potatoes, butter, milk, sour cream and seasoned salt) except I also boil the carrots (and if I remember) garlic. I use what ever cheese I have on hand (usually a mexican blend) and a can of drained corn. I use an electric mixer and blend as much as a I like. I find it a lot easier than a hand masher. Anyway, my husband prefers these over regular mashed potatoes and my 2 year old also likes it. It is now on our regular weekly menu. Thanks so much for the recipe!

Well ! ... I never!!! I've always made mashed potatoes the "ho--hmm" traditional way. Boring! But, this "Cowboy Mashed Potatoes" concoction recipe is a zappy pappy bell ringer! One comment regarding the addition of a jalapeno pepper while boiling the potatoes... it just adds a layer of flavor to the mix, without the eye popping heat, for those who don't like heat, that is. I love it, so I take the suggestion to heart and mouth of adding a 1/4 cup finely chopped peppers. After all, if you can't enjoy these smashing good potatoes while sitting around a campfire, you gotta get your heat from something else. Innovation buckaroos!

There are no words for the deliciousness of these potatoes; they are all kinds of awesome! And that's coming from a mashed potato purist (I've always been of the school of thought of why mess w/a good thing!). These ingredients intrigued me when I saw this recipe reviewed in the recent reviews and I decided to give them a try. Mr. LTH deemed these (and the accompanying meal) "the best meal he's eaten in awhile", which is high praise for him (his standard feedback is "yeah, I like it; it's good"). I couldn't STOP eating them and actually had THREE servings! I followed the recipe, but did not "measure" the potatoes and used 2/3 red (1/2 of them peeled, 1/2 w/skin on) and 1/3 white potatoes (no yellow at our grocery store). I also used 2 jalaps, simply because I'd picked up two at the store (I deseeded and demembraned them as Mr. LTH is Mr. Sissypants when it comes to spice). I didn't measure the cheese and I used a steamable bag of white/yellow corn. I'm not a fan of chunky potatoes, so I chose to mashed these in our KA, rather than the old school method for a smoother consistency (I also couldn't resist adding just a splash of milk). These are so good I WILL be serving them to our next dinner guests!
We added 1/2 cup minced hatch green chile peppers.

Great recipe! I changed it up quite a bit. I used a bag of Schwan's (now Yelloh) frozen mashed potatoes, milk, added a can of creamed corn, two chopped carrots, stewed/diced tomatoes (drained), grilled onions and mushrooms, crumbled bacon, threw in some extra French fried onions, mild jalapenos (canned), shredded sharp cheddar cheese, added dill to taste (tarragon would be good, too). Mine turned out like very thick potato soup--3 helpings for everyone! Will definitely make this again and again.
I made this recipe with more butter, 1/2 C instead of 1/4 C. I also added 1/4 C milk. It’s definitely a good, easy recipe. I’m not sure I’d make it again. I think it needs more flavor.

Red potatoes are a firmer, waxier potatoes. Good in lots of recipes but definitely NOT mashed potatoes. The waxy texture does NOT cream properly for mashed potatoes. Just be warned about this. if you want/like chunkier potatoes, not smooth and creamy this recipe will work fine for you.

Great, delicious! I added lemon juice and peeled the potatoes. Can't get yellow potatoes here, or white corn. Used Bell peppers. Yum, yum!
